mainTopic: Number of judges for appraisals of הקדש and for capital cases involving animals
overview: This amud works through the משנה's rules about how many judges are needed for appraisals and for capital cases. First, the גמרא gives three explanations of 'ערכין המטלטלין בשלשה.' The first two each need a small change to the משנה's wording. In רבי אבהו's explanation, the כהן collects a pledged ערך from a person's belongings: three appraisers for movable items and ten for land, because a mistake can happen whether property goes into הקדש or comes out. The גמרא then asks why the חכמים need the word 'כהן,' and asks how שמואל gets nine Israelites and one כהן from the ten mentions of 'כהן.' Both questions end with קשיא. A person is appraised like land when he says 'דמי עלי,' because he is valued like a slave, and a slave is compared to land. רבי אבין asks whether hair that is ready to be cut counts as cut or attached. The גמרא shows this is a dispute between תנאים, and then shows it does not have to match the dispute about grapes on the vine. Finally, the גמרא finds a source showing that an animal that lay with a man is judged by twenty-three. It then begins to examine the source for the stoned ox, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pledging the valuation of a utensil means paying its value
steps.stepSummary: The first explanation of the משנה is built on a known ruling: if someone says 'the ערך of this utensil is upon me,' he pays the utensil's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who says, 'The valuation of this utensil is upon me,' must give its monetary value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the first explanation of 'ערכין המטלטלין' by quoting the rule about someone who pledges the ערך of a utensil. This ruling is the base for the next questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real ערך is a fixed amount set by the Torah for a person, based on age and gender. Here, though, the person used the word ערך about an object. According to this explanation, that is the case the משנה means: the utensil's value must be appraised, and that takes three people.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed 'valuation' set by the Torah that a person pledges to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: One who says: 'The valuation of this utensil is upon me'
phrases.notes: 'Upon me' means 'I take it upon myself to donate it to the בית המקדש.'

phrases.english: – gives its monetary value.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר: ״עֵרֶךְ כְּלִי זֶה עָלַי״ – נוֹתֵן דָּמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first explanation of the משנה's phrase, which was started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who pledges the ערך of a utensil pays the utensil's market value.

steps.title: Why does he pay the utensil's value?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind this ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a ערך pledge on a utensil turns into paying its value. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Objects have no Torah-fixed ערך, so we might have thought the words mean nothing and he owes nothing. The question asks why his words still create a duty to pay.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a ערך pledge on an object, which has no ערך, still makes him owe money.

steps.title: He knows utensils have no ערך, so he meant their value
steps.stepSummary: A person knows objects have no ערך. So he must have meant to pledge the object's money value.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person knows that a utensil has no valuation. So he made up his mind and spoke in terms of its value. That is why he gives its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we read the person's words based on what he must have meant. He knows a utensil has no ערך, so he surely meant its price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We assume a person does not speak for nothing. Since a literal ערך makes no sense for an object, his words are taken as a pledge of its value. Because the value has to be appraised, three judges are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He made up his mind and said

phrases.english: A person knows that a utensil has no valuation,
and he decided and spoke in terms of its value.
Because of this, he gives its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since he knows objects have no ערך, his words are taken as a pledge of the object's value.

steps.title: The משנה's wording does not fit this explanation
steps.stepSummary: If the case is a ערך pledge on an object, the משנה should have said 'ערכין של מטלטלין,' not 'ערכין המטלטלין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This phrase, 'valuations that are movable property'? It should have said 'valuations of movable property'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first explanation from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ערכין המטלטלין' sounds as if the ערכין themselves are the movable property. In this case, though, the ערך is said about a movable object, so 'of movable property' would fit better.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property (things you can carry, unlike land)

phrases.english: This phrase, 'valuations that are movable property'?
It should have said 'valuations of movable property'!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי ״עֲרָכִין הַמִּטַּלְטְלִין״? ״עֲרָכִין שֶׁל מִטַּלְטְלִין״ מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation from steps 1-3 on the basis of the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording does not exactly match a case of a ערך pledged on an object.

steps.title: Read the משנה as 'ערכין של מטלטלין'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the wording of the משנה to fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'valuations of movable property.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps its explanation and simply adjusts how the משנה should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case does not change. Only the wording is fixed, so that the משנה now plainly describes a ערך said about movable items.

phrases.english: Teach: 'valuations of movable property.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's wording seemed not to fit this case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'ערכין של מטלטלין,' and the explanation stands.

steps.title: Second explanation: paying a ערך with movable items
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting אבימי, says the משנה is about someone who hands over movable items to pay a ערך he owes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: It is about someone who sets aside movable property for his ערך.
steps.whatsHappening: A new explanation of the משנה is offered. Here the person really owes a ערך, and he pays it with objects instead of cash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the ערך is a real, Torah-fixed ערך. The objects given to pay it must be appraised to see how much they cover, and that is why three are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside or attaches property to something holy

phrases.english: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי:
It is about one who sets aside movable property for valuations.
phrases.notes: He owes a ערך and gives objects to cover it, so they need to be appraised.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אֲבִימִי: בְּמַתְפִּיס מִטַּלְטְלִין לַעֲרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה refers to movable property handed over to pay a ערך, which must be appraised by three.

steps.title: The wording does not fit this explanation either
steps.stepSummary: If the case is objects given for a ערך, the משנה should have said 'מטלטלין של ערכין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This phrase, 'valuations that are movable property'? It should have said 'movable property of valuations'!
steps.whatsHappening: The same wording challenge is now aimed at רב חסדא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the main subject is the objects that pay for the ערך. So the wording should put the movable property first: 'movable property of valuations.'

phrases.english: This phrase, 'valuations that are movable property'?
It should have said 'movable property of valuations'!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי ״עֲרָכִין הַמִּטַּלְטְלִין״? ״מִטַּלְטְלִין שֶׁל עֲרָכִין״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's explanation in the name of אבימי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording does not match a case where objects are given to pay a ערך.

steps.title: Read the משנה as 'מטלטלין של ערכין'
steps.stepSummary: Again, the גמרא answers by adjusting the wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'movable property of valuations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves רב חסדא's explanation by rereading the משנה to fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of the first two explanations need a wording change. The only difference is which wording each one requires.

phrases.english: Teach: 'movable property of valuations.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wording seemed not to fit this case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'מטלטלין של ערכין,' and the explanation stands.

steps.title: Third explanation: the כהן collects movable items or land
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the case is someone who pledged 'my ערך,' and the כהן collects payment from his property: movable items need three appraisers, land needs ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is about someone who says 'My valuation is upon me.' If the כהן comes to collect movable property from him, it takes three. If he collects land, it takes ten.
steps.whatsHappening: A third explanation is given. It fits the משנה's wording without any change, and it also explains why the משנה speaks of land separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a real ערך is owed, and the כהן collects it from the person's belongings. The items being collected are appraised by three if they are movable and by ten if they are land.

keyTerms.meaning: My valuation is upon me (I pledge my own ערך)

phrases.english: רבי אבהו said:
It is about one who says 'My valuation is upon me,'
and the כהן came to collect from him:
movable property – by three,
land – by ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third explanation of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When collecting a ערך, movable items are appraised by three and land by ten.

steps.title: Why three when property goes into הקדש?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי asks רבינא: three makes sense when taking property out of הקדש, but why is it needed when property is going into הקדש?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא from דיפתי said to רבינא: It makes sense that to take something out of הקדש we need three. But to bring something into הקדש, why do I need three?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges רבי אבהו's explanation. In his case, property is being collected for הקדש, not redeemed from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When property is redeemed from הקדש, a low price would harm הקדש, so careful appraisal is needed. When property is going into הקדש, רב אחא assumes there is no such worry, so why require three?

keyTerms.meaning: To take out of הקדש (redeeming it)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא from דיפתי said to רבינא:
It makes sense that to take out of הקדש we need three,
but to bring into הקדש,
why do I need three?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְאַפּוֹקֵי מֵהֶקְדֵּשׁ בָּעֵינַן שְׁלֹשָׁה, אֶלָּא לְעַיּוֹלֵי לְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שְׁלֹשָׁה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in רבי אבהו's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's requirement of three when collecting for הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for three appraisers seems to apply only when property leaves הקדש, not when it enters.

steps.title: A mistake can happen either way
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the reason is the same both ways. We need three because the appraiser might make a mistake, and that worry exists going in just as much as going out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is simple logic. What difference does it make to me whether it goes in or comes out? Why do we need three when it comes out? Because he might make a mistake. When it goes in, he might also make a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers that three appraisers are needed in both directions, since the reason is to avoid a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא thought the concern was only about harming הקדש when property leaves it. רבינא explains that the real concern is a wrong appraisal. A wrong price when collecting would also cause a loss to הקדש, so three are needed either way.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to me?
Perhaps he will make a mistake

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'ערכין המטלטלין' gets three explanations. The first two each need a wording change. רבי אבהו's explanation is a ערך collected from a person's property: three appraisers for movable items, ten for land. Three are needed even when property goes into הקדש, because a mistake can happen in either direction.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is logical reasoning:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי עַיּוֹלֵי, מָה לִי אַפּוֹקֵי?
phrases.english: what difference is it to me if bringing in, or taking out?
Taking out – what is the reason?
Perhaps he will err.
Bringing in, too – perhaps he will err.
phrases.notes: A mistake here could mean הקדש collects less than it is owed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סְבָרָא הוּא, מָה לִי עַיּוֹלֵי, מָה לִי אַפּוֹקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the same reason applies in both cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three appraisers are needed only to protect הקדש when property leaves it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three are needed whenever there is a risk of a wrong appraisal, whether property is going in or out.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים need the word 'כהן'?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: the word 'כהן' in the פסוק fits רבי יהודה, but why would the חכמים need it?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says one of the appraisers must be a כהן. רב פפא said to אביי: For רבי יהודה it makes sense, because the Torah writes 'כהן.' But for the חכמים, why do they need the word 'כהן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's opinion from the משנה. Then רב פפא challenges the חכמים, who don't require a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה requires a כהן among the appraisers, and the Torah does write the word 'כהן' in this פרשה. The חכמים say anyone can appraise, so that word seems to have no job in their view.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה, where רבי יהודה says one of the appraisers must be a כהן.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
this is why it is written "priest."
phrases.notes: For example, ויקרא 27:14.

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis,
why do they need "priest"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב כֹּהֵן אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן כֹּהֵן לְמָה לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה, רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's view that a כהן is not needed for appraisal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah writes 'כהן', so a view that does not require a כהן leaves the word with no purpose.

steps.title: The question on the חכמים stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the question is difficult and gives no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רב פפא's question by saying 'קשיא.' The question stands with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the challenge is real and has no answer here. It does not cancel the חכמים's opinion. It only means we don't have an explanation for the word 'כהן' in their view.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is not the same as 'תיובתא.' A קשיא leaves a question open, but the opinion is not rejected.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends step 12's challenge without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word 'כהן' is unexplained according to the חכמים, but their opinion still stands.

steps.title: Where do we learn nine and a priest for land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that land is appraised by nine and a כהן, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: land is appraised by nine people and a כהן. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable items need only three appraisers, but land needs ten, and one of them must be a כהן. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches both the number ten and the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: Land: nine and a priest.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for appraising land with nine Israelites and one כהן.

steps.title: שמואל: ten times 'priest' in the section
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says 'כהן' appears ten times in the פרשה. One teaches that a כהן is needed, and the rest form 'a limitation after a limitation,' which comes to include even non-כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The word 'כהן' is written ten times in the פרשה. One is for itself. The others are a limitation after a limitation, and a limitation after a limitation only comes to include. So even nine Israelites and one כהן are fine.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the source. He counts the ten times 'כהן' appears, and that gives us ten appraisers. Then he explains why only one of them has to be a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'כהן' would normally limit the job to כהנים. But there is a rule that one limitation piled on another limitation turns into an inclusion. So the extra mentions include ordinary Israelites, and only the first mention requires a real כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known דרשה rule: two limitations in a row come to include. It shows up in other places in ש״ס too.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Ten "priests" are written in the section,
phrases.notes: The פרשה is ויקרא 27, about valuing things given to הקדש.

phrases.english: one is for itself,
phrases.notes: He means this one teaches that there really must be a כהן.

phrases.english: those others are a limitation after a limitation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת,
phrases.english: and a limitation after a limitation comes only to include,
that even nine Israelites and one priest are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ten mentions of 'כהן' give ten appraisers. The first requires a כהן, and the rest, as a limitation after a limitation, include Israelites.

steps.title: Why not five priests and five Israelites?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges שמואל: by that logic, the mentions should switch back and forth, giving five כהנים and five Israelites.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן challenged this: Say instead that it means five כהנים and five Israelites!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן attacks the way שמואל counted the mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each new 'כהן' flips the meaning of the one before it, the result should go back and forth: כהן, Israelite, כהן, Israelite, and so on. That would give half and half, not nine Israelites and one כהן.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan challenges it:
Say: five priests and five Israelites?
phrases.notes: Each 'כהן' undoes the one before it, so they would switch back and forth and end up half and half.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's derivation in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading of nine Israelites and one כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using the limitation-after-limitation rule one step at a time should give alternating results, so five and five.

steps.title: The challenge to שמואל stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits רב הונא's question is difficult and gives no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion with 'קשיא.' רב הונא's question stands with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty is with how שמואל's derivation works. The משנה's ruling of nine and a כהן is still the הלכה, even though this question has no answer.
steps.whatToRemember: Land is appraised by ten people, and one must be a כהן. שמואל learns this from the ten mentions of 'כהן,' but the question of why it isn't five and five stays open.

phrases.english: It is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends step 16's challenge without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling of nine and a כהן stands, but the question on שמואל's derivation is left open.

steps.title: Can a person become holy?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a person is appraised like land. The גמרא asks how a person could be הקדש at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And a person is like them. But can a person become holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and questions how it could happen. This sets up רבי אבהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Appraisal is needed when something is given to הקדש. A human being can't be made holy like an object, so it's unclear what appraisal the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: Like them / in the same way
Is it? (a question word in Aramaic)

phrases.english: And a person is like them.
Is a person holy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a person is appraised like land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person cannot become הקדש, so there seems to be nothing to appraise.

steps.title: The case is 'my value is on me'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the משנה means someone who says 'דמי עלי,' pledging his own value to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The case is someone who says, 'My value is upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers by explaining the case. The person himself does not become holy. He promises to give his value in money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is not הקדש. He takes on a duty to pay his money value, so we have to figure out how much he is worth.

keyTerms.meaning: My value is upon me (a pledge to pay one's market value)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'דמי עלי' with 'ערכי עלי' from step 9. A ערך is a fixed amount set by the Torah. 'דמי' means what he is actually worth, so he has to be appraised.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
It is where one says, "My value is upon me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בְּאוֹמֵר דָּמַי עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by defining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say a person himself becomes holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The person pledged his money value, and that value is what gets appraised.

steps.title: A ברייתא: valued like a slave, and a slave is like land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי אבהו: someone who says 'דמי עלי' is valued like a slave in the market, and since a slave is compared to land, ten appraisers are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Someone who says 'My value is upon me' is valued like a slave being sold in the market. And a slave is compared to land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבי אבהו. It also explains why a person needs the same ten appraisers as land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the 'דמי עלי' case really involves appraisal, using a slave's market price. Since the הלכה compares a slave to land, the appraisal uses land's rule of nine and a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Is compared (treated the same in halacha)

steps.whatToRemember: A person who pledges 'דמי עלי' is valued like a slave. A slave is compared to land, so ten appraisers are needed, one of them a כהן.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
One who says, "My value is upon me"
is appraised like a slave sold in the market.
And a slave is compared to land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's case in step 19 and explains why ten appraisers are needed.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's explanation that the משנה means 'דמי עלי,' which needs ten appraisers
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying such a person is valued like a slave, together with the rule that a slave is compared to land

steps.title: How many appraisers for hair ready to be cut?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין asks whether consecrated hair that is ready to be cut counts as already cut (three appraisers) or still attached (ten appraisers).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין asked: hair that is ready to be cut, how many appraisers does it need? Is it like hair that was already cut, so three are enough? Or is it like hair still attached to the body, so ten are needed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין raises a new question that grows out of the last step: a person is valued like land and needs ten appraisers, but what about his hair that is ready to be cut?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable things are valued by three judges, while a person, who is compared to land, is valued by ten. Hair that is ready to be cut sits in between: it is still attached, but it is about to come off. The question is which side it belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a real question that he did not know the answer to

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin asked:
Hair that is ready to be cut, by how many appraisers is it valued?
Is it like hair that was already cut, and so valued by three?
Or is it like something still attached, and so valued by ten?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that a person, being like land, is valued by ten, and asks about his hair that is ready to be cut.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hair ready to be cut counts as cut (three appraisers) or attached (ten appraisers).

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the question is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about consecrating a slave shows that whether ready-to-cut hair counts as cut is a dispute between the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone consecrates his slave, there is no מעילה with the slave. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: there is מעילה with his hair. And we hold that they argue about hair that is ready to be cut. Learn from this that it is a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer רבי אבין's question, and finds that תנאים already argue about this exact point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion treats the slave's ready-to-cut hair like his body, so there is no מעילה with it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל treats it like hair that was already cut, a separate movable item, so there is מעילה with it. So the answer to רבי אבין depends on which תנא you follow.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates something to הקדש
There is מעילה: someone who benefits from it has misused holy property
We hold, we have it as an established fact

steps.whatToRemember: Whether hair that is ready to be cut counts as already cut is a dispute between תנאים.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת עַבְדּוֹ – אֵין מוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: One who consecrates his slave: there is no מעילה with him.
phrases.notes: If someone uses or benefits from the slave, he has not misused holy property.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
There is מעילה with his hair.
And we hold
that they argue about his hair that is ready to be cut.
Learn from this.
phrases.notes: What we learn is that רבי אבין's question is exactly what these תנאים argue about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבין's question by showing that it is already a dispute in a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It depends on the תנאים: the first תנא treats ready-to-cut hair as attached, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל treats it as already cut.

steps.title: Suggesting this dispute matches the dispute about laden vines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the hair dispute is the same as the dispute between רבי מאיר and the חכמים about vines full of grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say these תנאים argue the same way as those תנאים. As we learned: רבי מאיר says there are things that are like land and yet are not like land, and the חכמים do not agree with him. How so? 'I gave you ten vines full of grapes,' and the other says, 'There were only five.' רבי מאיר makes him liable, and the חכמים say: anything attached to the land is like the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison: maybe the hair dispute is just another version of a known dispute about grapes on the vine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of the vines, a person admits part of the claim. Normally that requires a שבועה, but claims about land do not. רבי מאיר requires the שבועה, so he treats the grapes like movable property, while the חכמים say whatever is attached counts as land.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say: the גמרא proposes an idea it will test
תנאים, the Sages of the משנה period
Makes him liable (here, to take a שבועה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר's 'liable' here means liable to take a שבועה for admitting part of the claim, not liable to pay.

phrases.english: Let us say these תנאים argue like those תנאים.
As we learned in a משנה: Rabbi Meir says:
phrases.notes: שבועות 42b.

phrases.english: There are things that are like land
and yet are not treated like land,
and the חכמים do not agree with him.
How so?
Someone claims: 'I handed you ten vines full of grapes,'
and the other one says: 'There were only five'.
Rabbi Meir makes him liable,
phrases.notes: Liable to swear, the way someone who admits part of a claim must swear.

phrases.english: and the חכמים say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְחוּבָּר לַקַּרְקַע הֲרֵי הוּא כַּקַּרְקַע.
phrases.english: Anything attached to the land is like the land.
phrases.notes: And there is no שבועה on claims about land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the dispute found in step 22 and tries to link it to a known משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the hair dispute and the vines dispute are really the same dispute.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבועות about ten vines full of grapes.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא: the vines case is about grapes ready to be picked
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that the vines dispute is about grapes ready to be picked: רבי מאיר says they are like picked grapes, and the חכמים say they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: we are dealing with grapes that are ready to be picked. One Sage holds they are like picked grapes, and the other Sage holds they are not like picked grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the comparison by explaining what exactly רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about in the vines case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know the grapes are ready to be picked, the vines dispute looks just like the hair dispute: is something ready to come off treated as already off? That is why the גמרא thought the two disputes were the same.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
We are dealing with grapes that are ready to be picked.
One Sage holds they are like picked grapes,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds they are not like picked grapes.
phrases.notes: These are the חכמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison from step 23 by showing the vines dispute is about grapes ready to be picked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the vines case, רבי מאיר treats grapes ready to be picked as already picked, and the חכמים do not.

steps.title: Grapes get worse on the vine, but hair keeps getting better
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: even רבי מאיר could agree that hair is not like cut hair, since grapes lose value on the vine while hair gains value as it grows.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, you can even say it fits רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר only said this there, because the longer you leave the grapes, the worse they get. But his hair, the longer you leave it, the better it gets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea that the two disputes are the same, by showing a real difference between grapes and hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats ripe grapes as already picked because leaving them on the vine only hurts them, so they are really 'done'. Hair is different: leaving it on makes it longer and worth more, so even רבי מאיר could say it still counts as attached. So the hair dispute is not simply the vines dispute again.
steps.whatToRemember: Grapes ready to be picked only get worse on the vine, so רבי מאיר treats them as picked. Hair keeps improving as it grows, so the two disputes do not have to match.

phrases.english: No, you can even say it follows Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: He means the opinion that ready-to-cut hair is still attached can fit even רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir only said it there, with the grapes,
because the longer you leave them,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: the worse they get.
But his hair,
the longer you leave it,
the better it gets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in steps 23–24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the hair dispute and the vines dispute are the same. The hair dispute itself from step 22 still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Grapes lose value on the vine, so they are treated as picked. Hair gains value as it grows, so even רבי מאיר could treat it as still attached.

steps.title: The משנה makes no distinction between male and female
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line on דיני נפשות and observes that it treats a רובע זכר and a רובע נקבה the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says capital cases, including an animal that lay with a person, need twenty-three judges. It says this without any exception, so it makes no difference whether the animal lay with a man or with a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section on the משנה's line about capital cases and points out that the משנה does not split the animal case into male and female. This observation sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the משנה speaks without any exception, both the case of a man and the case of a woman need twenty-three judges, and the animal is killed in both. Once this is said, the גמרא needs a source for each case.

keyTerms.meaning: Capital cases, where a life is at stake
The משנה teaches it without any exception
An animal that had relations with a person

phrases.english: Cases of capital law, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The 'etc.' covers the rest of the line, which includes an animal that lay with a person.

phrases.english: It teaches categorically,
there is no difference whether it copulated with a male
and no difference whether it copulated with a female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after the discussion of appraising consecrated hair and grapes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule of twenty-three judges for an animal involved with a person applies equally to male and female cases.

steps.title: The female case has a verse, but where is the male case?
steps.stepSummary: The killing of an animal that lay with a woman is written in the פסוק. The גמרא asks for the source for an animal that lay with a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of a woman is fine, because the תורה says, 'You shall kill the woman and the animal.' But where do we learn the case of an animal that lay with a man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the female case has a clear פסוק and asks for the source for the male case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a woman names the animal directly. For a man who lets an animal lie with him, the גמרא knows of no פסוק that says this outright, so it needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Granted, one that copulated with a female,
as it is written:
"And you shall kill the woman and the animal."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:16

phrases.english: But one that copulated with a male,
from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the male case that step 26 showed the משנה includes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that an animal that lay with a man is killed and judged by twenty-three.

steps.title: A verse not needed for its plain case teaches the male case
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כל שכב עם בהמה' is not needed for the man who actively lies with an animal, so it is applied to the man who is lain with. Because it uses the word שוכב, the two cases are compared, and both need twenty-three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה says, 'Whoever lies with an animal shall be put to death.' The man who actively lies with an animal is already taught elsewhere, so this פסוק is used for the man who lets an animal lie with him. The תורה still used the word 'lies' to compare the two: just as the man who lies with an animal is judged, together with his animal, by twenty-three, so too the man who is lain with is judged, together with his animal, by twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source. A פסוק that is not needed for its plain case is moved to the case of the man who is lain with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule of אם אינו ענין: if a פסוק would only repeat something already taught, we apply it to a new case. The תורה kept the wording שוכב on purpose to create a היקש, so the נשכב gets every law of the שוכב, including that the animal is killed and that the case needs twenty-three judges.

keyTerms.meaning: If the פסוק is not needed for its own case, apply it to another case
The man who actively lies with an animal
The man who lets an animal lie with him
A comparison the תורה makes between two cases so they share the same laws
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: An animal that lay with a man is killed and judged by twenty-three. This comes from 'כל שכב עם בהמה' through אם אינו ענין, together with a היקש of נשכב to שוכב.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Whoever lies with an animal shall be put to death."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:18

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of the one who lies,
phrases.notes: The man who lies with an animal is already covered by another פסוק, ויקרא 20:15.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of the one who is lain with.
And the Merciful One expressed it in the language of 'lies,'
to compare the one lain with to the one who lies:

phrases.aramaic: מָה שׁוֹכֵב – הוּא וּבְהֶמְתּוֹ בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה,
phrases.english: just as with the one who lies, he and his animal are judged by twenty-three,

phrases.aramaic: אַף נִשְׁכָּב – הוּא וּבְהֶמְתּוֹ בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: so too the one lain with, he and his animal are judged by twenty-three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְשׁוֹכֵב, תְּנֵיהוּ עִנְיָן לְנִשְׁכָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמות 22:18, applied through אם אינו ענין to the נשכב and compared by היקש to the שוכב, so both he and his animal are judged by twenty-three.

steps.title: The stoned ox is judged by twenty-three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a שור הנסקל needs twenty-three judges, because the פסוק links the ox's death to its owner's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox that is to be stoned is judged by twenty-three, as the תורה says, 'The ox shall be stoned and also its owner shall be put to death.' The ox dies the same way the owner would, so its case is judged the same way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's next line about the ox that killed a person and quotes the source the משנה gives. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה reads 'וגם בעליו יומת' as making the ox's death like the owner's death. A person's capital case needs twenty-three judges, so the ox's case does too.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that killed a person and is sentenced to stoning
The ox's death is judged like the owner's death

phrases.english: An ox that is to be stoned is judged by twenty-three,
as it is stated:
"The ox shall be stoned and also its owner shall be put to death."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:29

phrases.english: As the death of the owner,
so is the death of the ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה, about the ox that kills.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שור הנסקל is judged by twenty-three, learned from 'וגם בעליו יומת': the ox's death is like the owner's death.

steps.title: אביי asks how we know the verse means this
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא how we know that 'וגם בעליו יומת' comes to teach that the ox's death is like the owner's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: How do we know that the words 'and also its owner shall be put to death' are meant to teach that the ox's death is judged like the owner's death?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the משנה's reading of the פסוק and asks what proves that this is its message.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וגם בעליו יומת' could be read simply as a statement about the owner's punishment. אביי wants proof that they also set the ox's trial equal to the owner's trial, which is the basis for the ox needing twenty-three judges.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what it comes to teach

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
From where do we know that this "and also its owner shall be put to death"
is to teach that as the death of the owner, so is the death of the ox
that it comes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's reading of 'וגם בעליו יומת' as comparing the ox's death to the owner's death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could be teaching only about the owner's punishment. Nothing obviously shows that it sets the ox's trial equal to the owner's.
